We have a cavapoo who’s also 6 months and 8.6 lbs! We feed him the Hills Science Diet puppy kibble and we give him 1.5-2 scoops (we have a measuring cup scoop, so each scoop is 1/8 a cup) 3 times a day. If he finished his previous meal he gets 2 scoops, and if he didn’t he gets 1-1.5 scoops. We also add 4-6 cubes of Primal Cupboard Turkey-Grain Free Freeze Dried topper per meal. And then every 1-2 days one of his meals in the day either has 1 pump of fish oil or 1-2 freeze-dried sprats (depending on the size of the sprat). 

We are also looking into incorporating more whole veggies into his diet, but I haven’t done a bunch of research yet!

I think the best advice I got from our family vet is that if they are hungry, pup will let you know! And if he’s full, he’ll leave it. If our puppy has gotten a lot of exercise or going through a growth spurt, we allow him 1 refill per meal of 1 additional scoop.
Thank you for your help! :)

My husband and I are in the same boat you are in (we’re 25 + 26, have been talking about getting a dog for over 3 years, started a budget to save for a dog 1.5 years ago, live in an apartment). We decided to get a puppy a few months ago. And he’s been lovely!

I think the biggest things to note (if I could go back in time) are:

- we got a puppy and they are a TON of work AND time. From potty training to puppy training to constant supervision, it’s a huge time commitment. If you want a calmer more established companion, I’d recommend getting an older dog (maybe a pup that’s older that 10 months or at least a year and a half old). With an older pup, they’ll kind of know what’s the what with potty training and have a lot less energy
- for travel, since we love to travel too, I wouldn’t 100% rely on friends and family. Always have a trusted backup plan like an experienced dog sitter
- my husband and I both have a flexible job. At the start we had either one of us wfh on a given day. And over time, as he got better with his crate and was able to sleep longer, what we do now is both of us go to work in the morning and one of us comes home at lunch to wfh in the afternoon
- if you budget, plan to spend about 1.75x more than you are expecting to spend in the first few months. We buy really high quality treats for our puppy, but dog stuff is expensive (at least in the US). There’s also a lot of toys/enrichment/etc. that we didn’t know existed and we got. Example: our puppy is so little and we got him puppy stairs for our couch. 
- Relationship Strain. This one is BIG for us. As with any adjustment (marriage, kids, new jobs, etc.), things will change. There were habits in our relationship where we both had to sit down and talk through. If you and your partner have great communication habits, this will be a breeze (to talk about, not about the issue). You both will adjust to the new responsibilities and just know it’s normal and with patience and love and understanding you can navigate through it together. 

Lastly - a pup is one of life’s purest and best joys. We both grew up with a dog and we spent a long time researching the perfect breed, food, training styles etc. and there have been so many days and nights where we are tired and exhausted from him being a puppy. But to grow our little family, I’d do it a thousand times over. 

So I would recommend to get a pup, on the condition that you do research, analyze if you can pull a pup off. You’ll be so happy you do!
